newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B index ends up on A share rises.
newsitem.headline: China's B index ends up on A share rises.

text.p: China's B share index ended up on Monday on speculative domestic buying in low-priced shares encouraged by sharp rises in the A share markets, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index was up 0.591 points or 0.81 percent to 73.527 points on turnover of $7.6 million compared with $6.3 million last Friday.
Shanghai's A share index rose 34.045 points or 2.7 percent to 1,293.362 points on turnover of nine billion yuan ($1.1 billion).
Shanghai brokers said prevailing rumours of financial restructuring stirred active buying in low-priced shares with poor results records on both the A and B share markets.
"The B market will continue to follow the movements on the A share market as domestic investors dominate trading in the short term," one broker said.
Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.018 or 7.82 percent to $0.248 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Bicycle maker Shanghai Phoenix followed, also on speculative buying, gaining $0.014 or 7.52 percent to $0.200 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shenzhen's B share market has been closed since Friday in line with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange's Easter holiday. Trading will resume on Tuesday morning.
However, the exchange system indicated that 224,000 B shares worth HK$1.1 million ($142,000) were traded on Friday morning, pushing the index up 0.42 points to 162.56 points.
Friday's transactions would be carried over to Tuesday, an exchange statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said.
"Because of technical reasons, the B share trade on March 28 is effective, and will be included in the next trading day," the statement said but gave no details.
Shenzhen's A share index added 11.74 points or 2.63 percent to close at 458.49 points. Turnover was 10.8 billion yuan against Friday's 10.5 billion yuan.
